messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired: SEV2 - inference-eu-high-latency (INC-20230). Routing: hosted API EU. Trigger: 95th p50 token latency > 3s for 5m.

pagerbot: paging -> @maya (primary on-call). escalation in 2m if no ack.

maya: Acked. I'm on it — looking at dashboards.

maya: initial customer impact: multiple mid-market customers reporting degraded response times (3-8s). No 5xx yet.

sre-oncall: thanks @maya. Can you check autoscaler and KV cache hit rate? I saw a small drop in kvcache evictions earlier.

maya: running quick checks: `curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/series?query=inference.latency.p50.region=eu`

maya: kvcache evictions spiked ~10:12Z, batch sizes dropped. Autoscaler shows no recent scale-ups for dedicated pools.

eli: FYI I'll be rotating onto this shift in ~10m. If this looks like pool capacity, I can take handoff for the rotation window.

maya: good note. I can triage for 10m and then handoff to @eli. Steps I'm taking now: 1) draining suspicious hosts 2) check autoscaler logs 3) try config rollback for batching.

sam: tagging runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency (runbook section: 'eviction-induced latency').

maya: found noisy tenant causing large seq lengths in hosted EU. Correlating traces.

maya: mitigation attempt 1: blackhole heavy tenant traffic with temporary routing rule. Command: 
```
redwoodctl route update --block-tenant tenant-42 --region eu
```

pagerbot: action applied by @maya: route update accepted.

maya: early signal: p50 dropped from 3.4s -> 1.2s for affected endpoints. Good. Still watching for side effects.

sre-oncall: solid. Prepare a short customer-facing blurb if this doesn't fully resolve in 20m.

maya: @eli will you take rotation handoff at 10:25Z? I'll document steps and handoff summary.

eli: yes I'll take it. Please post the brief summary and I'll confirm.

maya: Handoff summary: 
- Trigger: spike in kvcache evictions + noisy tenant large seqs -> p50 increase to ~3.4s
- Mitigation applied: temporarily blocked tenant-42 routing (see command above)
- Effect: p50 reduced to ~1.2s; no 5xx observed
- Next actions for oncoming oncall: monitor kvcache hit rate, watch for re-onboarding of tenant-42, consider graduated rate-limits on tenant if recurrence.
- Links: dashboards + traces: https://telemetry.internal/d/inf-eu | runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency

eli: got it. Taking ownership now. I'll keep a 5m cadence updates.

pagerbot: ownership transferred -> @eli. Incident state: acknowledged by @maya, owner @eli.

eli: 10:30Z: p50 stable ~1.1s. kvcache evictions trending down. Rolling window 15m looks okay.

eli: 10:40Z: reached out to product-support to notify impacted customers and to prepare a short postmortem if tenant-42 needs permanent throttling.

maya: thx @eli. If you need me later for rollback context ping me.

eli: will do. If things stay stable I'll close this after a 30m quiet window and update INC-20230.

sam: please include cost impact check later (bursting hosts spun up?) and note any dedicated pool delta.

eli: noted. adding to incident ticket.

eli: 11:00Z: quiet window passed, p50 stable <1.2s, no new evictions. Marking incident as mitigated. I'll keep the temporary block for 2 hours and then lift under controlled rollout.

pagerbot: mitigation logged by @eli. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

eli: Closing notes: mitigation effective; root cause likely noisy tenant causing KV cache churn + poor batching. Action items: formal follow-up with tenant to optimize sequence sizes, consider automated tenant rate limiting and kvcache protection heuristics. Assigned to @maya for follow-up and @sam for cost analysis.

incidentbot: INC-20230 updated: severity lowered to SEV3, assignees: maya, sam.

eli: thanks all. End of handoff. :white_check_mark:
